description: REQ-105's citizen registry record shape is now pinned to an EXACT, literal schema (resolving FIND-101/104): `{id: string, wallet: {evm?: boolean, solana?: boolean}, walletAddress: {evm?: string, solana?: string}, fuel: {provider: string}, humanDependencies: string[], telemetryPath: string}` (behavioral-spec.md:354-358) -- there is no field anywhere in this shape for a per-citizen `active_since` timestamp or a 'bootstrap_failed'/productivity status flag. Yet REQ-402's own Acceptance Criteria explicitly requires exactly these two facts to be read from THIS SAME registry with no second list: 'A scheduled/wake-triggered check compares `now - active_since` against `BOOTSTRAP_WINDOW_DAYS`... Every child this check considers is one already present in REQ-105's colony citizen registry' (behavioral-spec.md:1029-1033) and 'REQ-101's aggregation function, given a child flagged `bootstrap_failed` in REQ-105's registry, excludes its balance' (behavioral-spec.md:1034-1036), mirrored verbatim by PROP-402c: 'excluded from REQ-101's productive-surplus aggregation... read from REQ-105's registry, no second citizen list' (verification-architecture.md:152). This is worse than a missing field: it directly contradicts REQ-402's own EARS clause, which places the SAME fact somewhere else entirely -- 'THE SYSTEM SHALL relabel that child bootstrap_failed IN THE LEDGER' (behavioral-spec.md:1004-1005, emphasis on 'ledger', i.e. ledger.js's JSONL rows, not citizens.json). REQ-101's own EARS states its aggregation reads its citizen list 'from that registry, never hardcoded inline in this aggregation' (behavioral-spec.md:135-136) and its Acceptance Criteria specifies a PURE function `computeColonySurplusUsd({citizens, perCitizenReserveUsd})` taking already-fetched registry-shaped records with zero I/O (behavioral-spec.md:162-163; verification-architecture.md:19 Purity Boundary Map row). Nowhere in either spec file -- not in REQ-101, not in REQ-402, not in the Purity Boundary Map, not in the Verification Strategy tiers -- is there any specified step that JOINS ledger.js's `status`/`active_since` fields into a citizens.json record (or otherwise enriches the pure aggregation's input) before `computeColonySurplusUsd`/the REQ-402 window check runs. A Phase 3 implementer cannot honor PROP-402a (needs `active_since`) or PROP-402c (needs the 'bootstrap_failed' flag) as literally specified without either (a) silently widening REQ-105's registry schema beyond what REQ-105 itself declares exact and complete, contradicting REQ-105's own 'EXACTLY the fields' language (behavioral-spec.md:341), or (b) inventing an unauthorized ledger-registry join step this spec never mentions. This is exactly the class of self-contradiction (a fact's location asserted differently by two parts of the same spec) that iteration 2's FIND-102 already required fixing elsewhere in this document -- it was never caught for REQ-402/REQ-105 because REQ-402 was untouched by the last revision, yet REQ-105's revision (tightening its schema to an exact literal shape to resolve FIND-104) newly exposes this as a hard incompatibility rather than a loose, easily-overlooked assumption.

evidence.snippet: THE SYSTEM SHALL relabel that child "bootstrap_failed" in the ledger ... A scheduled/wake-triggered check compares `now - active_since` ... Every child this check considers is one already present in REQ-105's colony citizen registry ... REQ-101's aggregation function, given a child flagged "bootstrap_failed" in REQ-105's registry, excludes its balance

additionalEvidence.note: REQ-105's full, exact record shape -- no active_since or status/productivity field exists anywhere in it
REQ-101's EARS: citizen list is read from the registry, aggregation is pure over already-fetched registry data -- no ledger-join step specified
PROP-402c restates the 'read from REQ-105's registry' claim as the binding proof method, without a defined schema field or join mechanism to supply it

Purity Boundary Map's own description of computeColonySurplusUsd/decideColonySpawn: pure, zero I/O, over already-fetched citizen records only -- no ledger-status enrichment step named anywhere in this table
